simple.meaning: מַטְמוֹן (maṭmôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a secret storehouse; hence, a secreted valuable (buried); generally money.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Genesis, Job, Proverbs, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Genesis 43:23. Its contexts include family.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַטְמוֹן (H4301).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַטְמוֹן (maṭmôwn) / H4301 is traced through Genesis 43:23, Job 3:21, Proverbs 2:4, Isaiah 45:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a secret storehouse; hence, a secreted valuable (buried); generally money
definitions.full: H4301. matmon מַטְמוֺן noun masculine hidden treasure, treasure ; — absolute מַטְמוֺן Gen 43:23 ; plural מַטְמֹנִים Jer 41:8 Prov 2:4 ; מַטְמוֺנִים Job 3:21 ; construct מַטְמֻנֵי Isa 45:3 ; ( hidden ) treasure Gen 43:23 (of money in sacks); מִסְתָּרים מַטְמֻנֵי Isa 45:3 (i.e. treasures now hidden in secret places, shall become spoil of Cyrus; || חשׁך אוצרות ), Jer 41:8 , appositive דבשׁ שֶׁמֶן שְׁעֹרִים חִמִּים ; in comparative Job 3:21 (longing for death more than for treasure), Prov 2:4 (wisdom sought for like treasure). טנא (√ of following; Phoenician טנא is set up, erect , also offer, present , according to DHM in MV 10, 983 ).

occurrences.englishText: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
Who long for death, but it doesn’t come;
if you seek her as silver,
I will give you the treasures of darkness
But ten men were found among those who said to Ishmael, “Don’t kill us; for we have stores hidden in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey.”
